item.title: Re: New SCP. Der Verlorene
item.content:encoded:
The problem is that seems to be just a single instance of a shellshocked soldier. With that as a given, there's little of interest here. You need to build more into the character than that; if he could be treated then he may give some interesting historical notes, even possibly describe the SCP that transported him through time.

Or he could have the ability to time travel himself, and the ability was triggered due to stress. even if it was a one-time ability, it could be fascinating to study him. If it's not, then he could be of help in exploring historical eras, possibly confirming details.

If you are going to keep him shellshocked, then you need to show what he can add to the knowledge of The Foundation. There has to be some sign of what caused him to time travel or it's just a neat idea.

In what seems to be a common theme today, this is just the beginning of an idea, and needs to be fleshed out somewhat or it's just The Foundation equivalent of a freak; he's going to be confined until he dies, possibly gets killed, and not really contribute anything.

item.title: Seeking review: Furry Clinic.
item.content:encoded:
A bullied person makes a clinic that turns people into their fursona counterparts, permanantly, and painfully, you won't be able to mingle in society.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Alright I think I can write a decent article this time, this would be my 5th attempt at a concept being approved, although I thought of many more I scrapped. So, yeah, a furry, gets bullied in his childhood so he decides to become a furry, and thinks that: "Every furry I know wants to be their character! I'll find a way to make this come true!" He experiments a while to finally make a clinic which anyone who enters comes out their fursona. Non-furries find it exceptionally hard to locate. Now a side affect of this surgery is well, the subjects immediately seek out the nearest furry, and try to force them in, once they do so, the subject will return to the place they last slept, and wake up with no memory of this, I intended to make the creator of the clinic realize what he had done, he had ripped families apart, because he thought he was helping them, in reality, he didn't.

item.title: Re: The Railyard To Everywhere
item.content:encoded:
This is not a bad idea, and has a lot of great detail. However, the biggest problem is that the intelligence that set this up is not even hinted at, no trademarks, company signage, or anything like that. This sounds like something that was expensive to create and maintain, and that requires some sort of intelligence, even if it's just company of some sort.

Basically, whoever set it up needs to be defined and given some explanation here.

Also, if there needs to be some form of security. If they can't control who comes in, they can control what people do there. Even if it's just an old man with a whistle, if they are worried enough about there cargo that they are willing to kill for it, then it makes no sense to not have some form of security.

Lastly, you may want to consider who they are doing business with. There is no such thing as a stop that's just a stop; why is there a junction on Earth, and who are they doing business with here? Even if they are restocking, how are they doing that?

Good skeleton; now flesh it out.

item.title: Re: Go For Gold! - Cars, Corpses, and Consumption!
item.content:encoded:
I have very mixed feelings about this. The core ideal is fine, but I'm morally obligated to point out that compulsion should be avoided.

The first two logs are good. The third is entirely too wordy and I think breaks the suspension of disbelief - O5 should have more control over itself and realize exactly what is happening - not break down into disorder and infighting.

The description is greatly improved but there's still a massive dangling thread in that 'bank account money' comes out of thin air, which can't really happen with such a computerized banking system we have today. I think there's room for cleverness in handling that can add verisimilitude to what is admittedly a rather wacky article. The asteroid bit is also entirely extraneous and I'm not sure what its purpose is.

The writing is certainly better than the original article, but I think I would still no vote. The logs add a lot but my opinion is soured by the third log. The ending still works as it did in the original article. As a rewrite, I think you're still a bit hamstrung by the original core idea and I'm not sure there's much that can be done to mitigate that without changing the article fundamentally.

item.title: Re: SCP-5832
item.content:encoded:
1) You don't need to make it an SCP; once it demonstrates anomalous attributes it's a given. Also, it feels that this has not been greenlighted but it already has a number.

2) The Red Paper Castle: It may be better to phrase it such that the red paper was transformed into a duplicate of the original castle. I know it's semantics, but it just feels better. You may want to go through and look for similar instances; there are a number of similarly bulky phrasing.

3) This is a good start, but it needs to be expanded upon. Do they have a history? Why did they automatically become enemies, with no apparent attempt at diplomacy? Where are they getting more paper to build the castle? If I put a pack of white paper near the castle, what would happen? Did they have a religion prior to the researcher? What form does that worship take?

Heck, what's the psychology of the castle dwellers? Is it based off real medieval people or an idealized form, such as the SCA? For that matter, why was it built in the first place, was it for a warg game or just to see what could happen?

Again, really cool start. Now flesh it out.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: SCP-5832

Downvote for me, sorry.

The concept is good and its core, the logs, was well done. As a general narrative I have no qualms.

But I think a lot of aspects from the Foundation got lost for no reason:

1- This is not Neutralized, since it still works, it is just depressed;
2- It shouldn't be in a Standard Containment, first because it is an SCP, secondly because it is Sentient and self-motile;
3- The description cuts right to "it Anderson's, so that's why it is anomalous", giving unnecessary context without describing it or it properties in any relevant way. It sounds like a Task Force report, not the finished article;
4- A lot of details on GOIs' activities that have no bearing in the story and I don't really care;
5- They do no test whatsoever, then someone wants to use it because why not.

Let me be clear, I have nothing against the Foundation deciding to use an anomaly whose effects are actually useful and understood enough for some safety and reliability. But without tests there is no safety and reliability in it. This thing is a frigging autonomous AI, it could do horrible shit out of the blue for unknown reasons, at the very least, without some tests.

Some logs could be those tests, by the way, at least some of them. A single dummy test isn't nearly enough, and even downplaying the dumb "lets fry D-Classes for cheap data"a surgeon just begs for tests with D-Classes that needed the surgery because of accidents and stuff.

As a general concept we already have SCP-2295 and, with a different area of work, SCP-1230. So the good parts aren't enough for not downvoting.

item.title: SCP Idea "Thunder"
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Happy(?)

Page Layout: Standard article with a death report and psychological analysis, and maybe a interview log

Elevator Pitch:

+ show block
– hide block

•The SCP consists of two parts, POI-628356 and SCP-XXXX

•SCP-XXXX Is a dog formerly named "Thunder", who was previously owned by the POI-628356. According to the article, POI-628356 is the 15 year old son of A Researcher at a random site (Still haven't decided) who, as mentioned above, owned SCP-XXXX

•SCP-XXXX had to be put down at a vet clinic due to complications from a brain tumor.

•The SCP itself is anomalous because despite being "Dead" It still exists and acts like a completely normal dog. It eats, poops, pees, drinks and can even be petted. However, The SCP is completely invisible to everyone Except POI-628356 and other dogs.

•The whole concept behind the SCP is the fact that despite being dead, SCP-XXXX is in a quite literal sense, always with The Person of interest. This article is more about the story than the SCP.

Central Narrative:

+ show block
– hide block

The Central narrative follows the aftermath of Thunder's death and the effect it has on POI-628356, as well as the results of seeing his dog "alive" again. The Psychological analysis and vet clinic report will be the main focus of the article, with the possible interview log between POI-628356 being a sort of closing addition to how much thunder meant to POI-628356 and how happy he is to be able to see his dog again, even if no one else can.


Hook/Attention-Grabber:
+ show block
– hide block

The Article is meant to be a happy and sad SCP article, and is mainly to play into the idea that "They're only gone if you think they are" In a literal sense.

item.title: SCP idea: Retroactive weight gain supplement
item.content:encoded:
A scam supplement that is advertised as causing weight loss but it actually rewrites your memories to make you only think you have lost weight. Use it too much and your memories start getting weird.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up a lot of space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Edit: Added the required template.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Page starts with basic containment procedures and a description. The main part of the narrative will be in the experiment log, which will reveal more about the effects of the SCP and may include interview logs with the test subjects.

Elevator Pitch: A scam supplement that is advertised as causing weight loss but it actually rewrites your memories to make you only think you have lost weight. Use it too much and your memories start getting weird.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The SCP is a weight loss pill that you can order a subscription to though an anomalous phone number. Each pill rewrites your memories a little bit to make you believe you lost weight after taking the pill. Since it does not actually cause weight loss in the present, you probably will actually gain weight without knowing it. The more pills that are taken the fatter you will believe you used to be and the further back in time it changes your memories. Eventually, you will be convinced that you have been morbidly obese your entire life before you started taking the pills. If you keep taking the pills past this point (I will call this the critical point for now), things start to get strange. The boxes that the pills come in have two languages on them. One is English (or whatever language you speak) and is all lies, and the other is an unknown language. After the critical point, you gain the ability to read the unknown language, which tells the truth about what the pills do, and you start to gain memories from before you were born of being something not human.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It is a weight loss pill that retroactively turns users into gluttony monsters in human form, or at least makes them think they are.

Additional Notes: I haven't decided yet how much it affects other people's memories or physical records like pictures. I haven't decided yet what happens if you stop taking the pills, though it probably depends on if you have passed the critical point or not. I may end up leaving it ambiguous if it is actually changing the past or just your memories.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: Re: It Will Not Leave
item.content:encoded:
Got a PM about this, stated I didn't like it and my review would be negative, was requested to look at this all the same. With that noted, here we go:

+ show block
– hide block

I'll be honest, I was rather immediately skeptical when I read that Adam and Samuel not only are childhood friends and joined police academy at the same time, but they were also recruited by the Foundation and placed on an MTF immediately. MTF agents are the Foundation's best of the best, and the teams are specialized for more than just generic combat—how on earth did both of these guys just immediately get put on an MTF team, let alone the same team?

The grief and sense of guilt pursuits Samuel to the point that starts to see Adam during his routine more often with time, to the point that jeopardizes other companions during some MTF operations. After a psychological test, he is given an amnestic to forget about his friend and stick to the MTF.

This is where I as a reader start to lose interest in a full draft of this. It strikes me as odd that no one bothered addressing Samuel's trauma until after he started jeopardizing operations—surely the Foundation would have had him attend counseling as soon as he returned from the original mission? The "psychological test" involving the amnestic just seems incompetent and negligent; even if Samuel asked for his memory to be erased, he shouldn't have been allowed to continue with his MTF duties. It's also a huge hit to Task Force morale if the way the Foundation handles grief is to just force people to forget and chuck them back into the field.

However, after some time without issues, during an intense MTF operation, Samuel provokes a containment breach as he claims that an unknown individual appeared to him.

At this point the plotline just feels too contrived for me to take it seriously. Given the Foundation's judgment lapses thus far, as a reader I react with more "well, what did they expect?" and not "oh no, that's terrible!"

Foundation demotes him and keeps him a study subject in order to prevent further failed operations, classifying Adam’s apparition as an SCP object.

I mean, I guess after two ill-advised doses of amnestics it's reasonable to guess that something anomalous is afoot, but I'm still wondering why Samuel didn't get any sort of therapeutic care during all of this.

Eventually, Samuel commits suicide.

I would downvote pretty immediately for this. It's overdramatic and entirely avoidable, and the usage of suicide as a plot point doesn't sit well with me. Granted, I myself headcanon the Foundation as extremely competent… if you really want to write a story where the Foundation thoroughly fails to help one of their personnel, I'm definitely not the right reviewer for such a piece.

An MTF operative from Samuel’s former MTF squad is recorded in a tapped phone call claiming that he has spotted Samuel in his garden and is afraid of reporting this to the Foundation.

Why would this MTF agent be scared of reporting that sighting? The Foundation can't do anything about what they don't know, and keeping knowledge of a potential anomalous effect secret would put everyone else the operative works with at risk.

Adam’s apparition to Samuel is not real. It is driven by strong feelings of guilt, grief and melancholy. […] So to avoid jeopardizing future operations, Foundation classifies it as an anomaly. Samuel’s sorrow becomes a memetic effect.

I have a very difficult time taking this seriously. Emotions and mental symptoms associated with traumatic events are very real and I can't see the Foundation treating this case as an anomaly. The justification of "they don't want to jeopardize future operations" doesn't make sense (unless Samuel is just too irreplaceable) since Samuel wouldn't mess up operations if he was allowed to take time away to mourn in peace. The sorrow becoming a memetic effect also seems odd since there's no specific information being transferred here. Mind-affecting maybe, but I'm not seeing the memetics relation.

It also seems weird that the Foundation would decide to write up an uncontainable anomalous phenomenon that would cause more panic, rather than just getting the MTF staff some therapy.

First, how even long-term friendship can deeply mark an individual;

This admittedly makes me curious as to why Adam and Samuel were placed on the same MTF team. They'd potential be emotional liabilities to each other. I can see why it has to be set up this way to commence the desired plot, but if the narrative focus on friendship is reliant on a contrived plot, the emotion might feel artificial and disingenuous.

and second, the HRM policy of the Foundation regarding its MTF operatives, and the perils of mental health mismanagement.

Given that the MTF agents are the best of the best, I have trouble believing that the Foundation would mismanage Samuel's care to such a disastrous degree. Again, the incompetence of the Foundation feels more like authorial meddling than something that I personally would believe, and the core theme is difficult for me to take seriously as currently presented.

As an aside, I admittedly have a lot of skepticism on this sort of story since I've volunteered at a psyc department, written a thesis on cancer patient trauma, and handled data for for a stress research lab. There's a wide body of research regarding grief and mourning (also one of my best friends lost a beloved dog recently. She says she still hears his barking sometimes. This isn't an abnormality) and the main roadblock I have is the Foundation being portrayed as, well… pretty clueless, it seems.

Again though, I tend to be more picky and demanding for scientific realism than most readers. There are plenty community members who enjoy stories where the Foundation messes up a lot; I just personally can't take those stories seriously enough to enjoy the read.

So far as suggestions for moving forward go, this is what I recommend:

  • change the role assignment for the two. MTF raises more eyebrows than, say, security personnel (would make sense for someone with police work in their resume) or field agent.
  • have the Foundation provide therapy for Samuel after Adam dies.
  • make it clear that Samuel asks to be put on the amnestics. Have it just be the one dose.
  • don't have the Foundation write up the anomaly. Maybe have the document be something that Samuel was writing up himself, believing that he was affected by an anomaly because his grief broke through the amnestics.
  • don't end the piece with Samuel's suicide.
  • if you want to have the Foundation be really struggling to provide mental health care, have there be a clear and believable reason why. Remote site that is dangerous and inhospitable to therapists who are used to working in offices? Stubborn refusal of Samuel to take the counseling sessions seriously? Etc.

I myself would have set this up as a tale. Do you really need to have this be an SCP article? You can consider writing a tale that has article inserts, like Revised Entry or Reality Check.

item.title: Re: Flashpoint Just league Dark
item.content:encoded:
It's up to interpretation but since DC is a multiverse, I'd think it's an alternative reality, not a reset (sorry). We may think it's a reset when really, Barry has simply jumped from one reality to another.

Compare it to endgame. In that, the Avengers travel to the past to take the infinity stones to the future. In doing so, they cause alterations to the past but the future remains unchanged. This is because, at the moment they go back in time, to preserve the flow of time, the universe creates an alternative universe. This is to prevent a paradox. You're no longer altering the past because it's no longer your past. The same can be said for JLD.

In Flashpoint, barry travels back and creates an alternative reality in which his mother survives and a whole loud of s*** goes down. In JLD, he's now doing it a fourth time.

Unfortunately, if you want to avoid paradoxes and have as much logic in time travel, it's got to be alternative worlds. Reset just isn't possible.

item.content:encoded:
How is everyone doing?

My name is Joel.

Anyways, why am I here? Well, you can probably thank the Youtube video blogger Ekhert's Ladder for that. I was watching one of his videos, and found myself here, obsessively reading entries. Some have been better than others, but there have been others that have been inspiring, creative, and even downright iconic (SCP-682, what I call The Plot Armor Reptile, SCP-1342, or what I call: What NOT to do to your Closest, Possibly Only Ally, SCP-1000 Bigfoot, SCP-2273, or what I call YOU MANIACS and YOU BLEW IT UP!!!, etc.).

As someone who loves themes that explores extraterrestrial life, alternate universe, running gags (again, SCP-682), and more emotional themes, such as hope and fear, and cruelty and morality (Foundation seems to be somewhat lacking in far the latter, and has ample amounts of in the one before that), the SCP multiverse is a fascinating medium for exploring such concepts. And yes, I'm a huge nerd, who will without hesitation make TV culture references.

I hope to write one or two entries, since it isn't like I don't have at least one idea for an SCP. As for whether or not I actually complete it is another matter, since I have hobbies in drawing/Photoshop/Illustrator, and more than occasionally in video games, and hope to go back to school, and begin a major Political Science next season. Not to mention I'd need to stop reading entries long enough to write something of substance!

Don't expect me to write any stories of gore and dark creatures in darkened hallways here to steal the souls of any Mobile Task Forces foolish enough to try to capture him, and disembowel any researcher foolish enough to refer to him by "it" or "SCP" though. Do expect content like an alternate instance of SCP-682 getting a cameo, and being dragged out, kicking, screaming, and shouting threats to something that doesn't consider it welcome. Because that is my sense of humor.

The only thing that seems to keep me up at night is on nights where I know that I have to get up early in the morning, but my brain won't SHUT DOWN ALREADY! Oddly enough, knowing that my part time job isn't enough to afford to move out, and that it will take at least two years to do something about it does not keep me up, even though it probably should.

item.title: Safe class SCP: The Wrong Chair
item.content:encoded:
The wrong chair is a chair that is impossible to remain seated in due to discomfort. If one remains seated anyway nearly harmless anomalous effects may occur.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Other (Simply a strange object)

Page Layout (Optional): Standard Format

Elevator Pitch: This is a chair, bench, or other form of seating that makes anyone that tries to sit there very uncomfortable with the idea of sitting there without any physical effects. It is not possible to contain, however, as it relocates via unknown means.

Central Narrative: The Wrong Chair almost always replaces damaged seating in seemingly random locations around the planet. It also has no uniformed appearance. Occasionally it will appear as an additional seat in a room instead of replacing a broken one. The Wrong Chair causes minor psychological distress to those seated on it until they move, but there is no lasting effects upon standing. If anyone manages to remain seated for more than 2 minutes and 37 seconds The Wrong Chair will disappear, leaving them to fall to the ground, or to land on top of the damaged seating The Wrong Chair formerly replaced. The Wrong Chair will always relocate within 24 hours, and always appears somewhere unobserved. In at least two cases it appeared when someone blinked, replacing a broken seat in the room they were in. ETC.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Simply enough this is just something bizarre but mostly harmless, yet impossible to contain.

Additional Notes: First try by me! People told me to submit the idea here from other locations.

item.title: Re: SCP IDEA: "Home"
item.content:encoded:
Hello and thank you for feedback!

The village was initially raided under the belief that it was a Sarkic village because of repostings of "flesh creatures" in the area. After the MTF goes missing, the foundation sends in a remote-controlled camera. They observe the inhabitants of the village but everyone seems to ignore the camera and nothing anomalous occurs. They decide to send in a D-Class, upon entering the people in the village transform into people resembling common city folk. After staying in the village for a while, the buildings start to transform into familiar buildings and the people become familiar. The D-Class is aware that the people aren't actually their family and friends but it just feels like its their true "home". The D-Class destroys the camera and radio. The foundation loses all contact. They further research but I haven't decided what else yet.

The village creates the anomalous effect to keep people inside the village. The village doesn't want people to leave for a unknown reason. Also the reason I picked nostalgia is to enforce the main idea of "home". The people don't want to leave because it brings them back to a better time in their life. It makes them feel at home.

Hello hello Duganist! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey. We're very happy to see new people excited to write for the format and deeply interested in the SCP Universe - especially since it seems you have quite the baggage of experience! If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

I liked it, although I should probably adjust my voting rubric for this series so that "well-written and engaging" isn't the sole criteria for an upvote.

The Navarro stuff didn't mean much to me, and most read like the "remember Budapest?" stuff in Avengers. I get that this was released sort-of in tandem with Alphabet stuff, but without a day-by-day calendar of when stuff was released four years ago, the only real option is to plough through one canon, then another, then another, or else be bogged down in a swamp of crosslinks. Not a critique, more an observation with the benefit of hindsight.

So far as criticisms go, the bit between Jason and Medea being captured and Anderson showing for murder would've probably benefited from some short intermediary piece. As it is, it feels a bit like it jumps from A to C. Additionally, I wasn't really vibing with the jumping perspectives; I get that it was anchored by "stuff Phineas set up," but it still felt disjointed.

Finally, I'm not sure what the deal is with Anderson declaring that he's going to restore the equilibrium to his relationship with Phineas when he's the one who disturbed it, but the author's definitely earned a measure of trust, so I'mma just roll with it.

item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlight ("The Boo Hag")
item.content:encoded:
Here's some crit:

[+] Open
[-] Close

a small collection of recovered documents and interviews.

I have no issue with the existence of these, but I'd like to know just how many recovered documents and interviews.

can be described as a “boo hag:”

The SCP can be called SCP-XXXX: Boo Hag, but I suggest not including the word "boo hag" in the article itself (at least not in the containment procedures or description) for the sake of staying clinical. Unless you want to mention that maybe it originated the legend of the "boo hag."

The reader is left to decide whether or not the man’s late wife was also Boo Hag and to question the origins of the “Daughter Hag.”

Given that this is the pitch and not the article itself, you should clarify what exactly the answer is and how you will reinforce this being hinted toward in the article

recovered documents

What exactly are these? The anomaly's diary?

I realize that choosing to write a humanoid SCP as my first article may be looked down upon

I think it's generally discouraged because they are hard to get right, but you seem to have a base to make a good one.

I'd critique more if I could, but you seem to have this concept pretty much down pat. I wish you the best of luck finishing it and would not mind to read the draft of this in the slightest.

item.title: Re: Echos eines Hoffest
item.content:encoded:
This activity went under the radar of the Foundation until a Turkish attendant was found dead after one of these events with the words "Deus Vult" engraved on his chest.

Sorry, is this just race based violence? If so, its a bad look. I don't really care if "in the 12th century this would be expected" or whatever… I just think its in bad taste.

There doesn't seem to be any narrative here, its just sorta a way of saying "wouldn't it be weird if Germany from the 1100s and modern day were to meet how different they would be?" Also I assume this is a period of history that is meaningful to you, which i respect, being fascinated with history myself… but without conflict and characters, and an arc, this won't work.

Foundation discovers anomaly -> Foundation does nothing -> then Foundation puts up fence, which doesnt work -> Foundation interviews monk that "seems to be responsible of these events" but isn't explained. End of article?

Its gonna read fairly dry, not to mention the way it starts is with normal every day Germans performing a hatecrime in a country that has ALOT of racial tension with its ethnically Turkish residents. So, I feel this whole part of the idea is gross and you should cut it.

item.title: Re: Dr Cheese SCP-5672 idea.
item.content:encoded:
Here's some crit:

[+] Open
[-] Close

skeletons labelled A,B and C.

This is unclear, do they have the letters A, B, and C painted onto them or is this the designation given to them by the Foundation? If it is the latter, they would typically be called something like SCP-XXXX-A, SCP-XXXX-B, and SCP-XXXX-C, or ditto but with numbers instead of letters (but that's more of personal preference.)

extremely indestructible

This implies the existence of a weak indestructibility. Just say something like, "invulnerable to damage" or simply, "indestructible."

except to electricity ranging from two thousand to four thousand (2000-4000) volts.

Is there any reason for this or is it just a convenient thing to keep them contained?

but no nuclear bomb/accident has occurred in the UK.

Ok then why is it there? You don't need to have a reason explicitly stated in the article, but you as the author should know exactly why there is caesium-135 and strontium-99 in small traces near a cave entrance.

The Story with these anomalies is that they were found in a cave in outer London

That may be a backstory, but it isn't a narrative. So far your anomaly seems a bit all over the place: a bit about them being royal, a bit about how it could be a publicity stunt (how would that even be possible considering the Foundation has them in containment?), a nudge towards a nuclear accident, and them being vulnerable to electricity for no reason.

They all have 3 things in common.

Is there a reason they need to have 3 things in common?

use their abilities for the good of the world

This is the only time this is brought up and is weird considering they are in Foundation custody so how do they do anything for "the good of the world."

which were thought to be obtained by strange minerals and substances in a cave under London.

This is your pitch, not the article itself, did they or did they not gain their abilities from this cave? If you want to have it be unsure in the article write down in this post something along the lines of, "they gained their abilities from this cave because blank and I will have that hinted at in the article through blank."

This is very rough, you have a bunch of ideas that seem all over the place and your central narrative doesn't seem to exist. You hint at just about everything and have no concrete "this is what and where the anomaly does, is, and came from" and are lacking a "this is what happens in the article itself." It seems like you have a million half-baked ideas in this pitch, pick a single backstory, a single thing they do over the course of the article, and remove all of the maybes in this pitch.
